passages.provision_quote: On receipt of a report of the existence of a homeless encampment, a city or town shall notify the owner to remove the owner's tent, structure or other personal property from the area in which the encampment is located. If removal does not occur within twenty-four hours after the order to remove the property, the city or town shall claim the property and retain the property for a period of fourteen days, during which the owner may claim the owner's property.
passages.note: Bill text sets a notice-then-property-removal process for homeless encampments; no criminal charge attaches to public camping itself under this section.
House Third Reading vote page; Montenegro voted Yea on final passage of this single-subject bill.

rows.reasoning: SB 1413 (2023) requires a city or town to notify an encampment's occupant to remove tents/structures within twenty-four hours, then claim and ultimately dispose of unclaimed property after fourteen days — a graduated-warning, civil (property-removal) mechanism matching 'Prohibiting encampments on public property, enforced through graduated warnings and civil penalties,' without criminalizing public camping itself. Montenegro voted Yea on House Third Reading (31-27-1-0-1), a final-passage vote on this single-subject bill.
